title: Structured Kernel Surrogate Models for Multimodal Attribution
abstract: arXiv:2611.13198v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study the problem of cross-sample modality attribution, which involves measuring how one modality in one sample affects the learning outcome in other multimodal samples. This problem is crucial in a multimodal system because a data modality (such as a text description) may be redundant for one sample (a self-explanatory image), but the same data modality would otherwise be uniquely informative for another sample, or informative when combined with other modalities. Prior work focuses on influence estimation at the level of one sample, and it remains an open question how one should capture the interactions across both samples and modalities. To capture scenarios like the above, we propose structured kernel surrogate models, which are surrogate mappings from both samples and modalities to the prediction outcome when they are trained together. translated_title: 用于多模态归因的结构化核代理模型
translated_abstract: 我们研究了跨样本模态归因问题，即测量一个样本中的某种模态如何影响其他多模态样本的学习结果。这个问题在多模态系统中至关重要，因为某种数据模态（例如文本描述）对于某个样本（例如自身就能解释的图像）可能是冗余的，但同样的数据模态对另一个样本来说却可能是唯一的信息来源，或者需要与其他模态结合时才具有信息价值。先前的工作主要集中在单样本级别的影响估计上，如何捕捉跨样本和跨模态的交互仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。为了应对上述场景，我们提出了结构化核代理模型，这是一种在联合训练时从样本和模态到预测结果的代理映射。我们设计了一种算法SKS，该算法应用具有结构化复合结构的核岭回归（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 提出结构化核代理模型及SKS算法，利用结构化核岭回归捕捉样本间与模态间的交互作用，首次解决多模态系统中的跨样本模态归因问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Structured Kernel Surrogate Models with the SKS algorithm, using structured kernel ridge regression to capture interactions across both samples and modalities, thereby solving the novel problem of cross-sample modality attribution in multimodal systems.
